title: Google Gemini evaluation error triage
summary: Determines whether a Google Gemini evaluation failure can be triaged from verified documentation. Product-specific diagnosis and remediation remain UNKNOWN until the evaluation workflow and replacement source are identified.
prerequisites: Access to the failed evaluation attempt and the evidence it produced
The name of the Google product or service used for the evaluation
The original cited-source record, including its title and prior URL

sections.title: Immediate answer
paragraphs: Can an intermediate practitioner safely apply product-specific error remediation from this guide now? No. The supplied material does not identify whether the failed evaluation used the Gemini API, Vertex AI model evaluation, or another Google workflow. Error meanings, diagnostic procedures, and corrective actions are therefore UNKNOWN and are omitted rather than guessed.

First identify the product or service shown by the failed attempt and retain the error evidence exactly as produced. If the product cannot be identified, stop and ask the workflow owner for the request context or evaluation record. Do not select remediation from a similarly named Google service.

Next match the identified workflow to first-party documentation. If the documented scope does not clearly match the workflow, or the source cannot be opened, record that the match is CANNOT VERIFY and ask the workflow owner or Google support channel appropriate to that service for the applicable documentation before changing or retrying the workflow.

sections.title: Source correction and triage boundary
paragraphs: The cited source record that triggered this update is content/resources/provider-workflows/google-gemini-evaluation-error-triage.json, supplied as an unregistered publisher that was never verified. The supplied record contains no external source title, old URL, replacement URL, or previous verification date. Whether an underlying source moved or merely passed its review cadence is UNKNOWN.

This source defect affects every product-specific error explanation, diagnostic step, remediation instruction, and success criterion that would depend on the missing citation. Those details are omitted until the original citation and an applicable first-party replacement can be compared. The existing resource text was not supplied, so which material was unaffected and should remain verbatim is also UNKNOWN.

To complete the correction, obtain the original source entry and open its prior URL. If the prior URL fails, retain evidence of that failure and locate a first-party replacement through the applicable Google documentation rather than assuming that one of the candidate sources below is equivalent. Compare the old and replacement guidance claim by claim. If the old content is unavailable, do not assert that the replacement preserves it; request an archived copy or the prior editorial record.

After the comparison, change only claims whose supporting guidance moved or changed. If a claim cannot be mapped to the replacement source, mark it UNKNOWN and omit it. If an attempted corrective action still fails, preserve the resulting evidence, stop repeating the action, and follow the first-party recovery or escalation guidance for the identified service.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: A completed source correction should produce four pieces of evidence: the exact Google evaluation workflow, the original cited-source metadata, an accessible first-party replacement source, and a claim-level record of what changed. Because the original resource and citation were not supplied, that evidence is currently incomplete and successful correction is UNKNOWN.

Verify readiness by opening the old and replacement URLs over HTTPS, confirming that the replacement addresses the same Google workflow, and checking each affected instruction against the replacement text. If either URL cannot be opened or the scopes differ, record CANNOT VERIFY and return the item for source research instead of publishing product-specific remediation.

Verification of an actual evaluation recovery requires the product-specific output produced by the corrected procedure. That output could not be established from the supplied material, so no evaluation result, request status, log entry, or other success signal is asserted here. Obtain the applicable first-party documentation and define the expected evidence before treating a retry as successful.
